svg.data-line-read-by: Claude, 2026-10-31, on the page image: line 4 of the column counted from its top. Every column of the page begins on the same ruled line and no line above this one is blank, so the count is the same whether blank lines are counted or not; Charles Loder's leningrad-codex-tei at commit 15405046fe811d4e1064a7ebcd7cb92261ce72db numbers it line 4 too
svg.data-combined-source: UXLC 2.6, as copied into in/UXLC-39/: Exodus 19:23, atoms 5 to 10 of 20, the whole line; the verse has one cantillation, so the UXLC's text is the combined transcription; Ben has changed nothing in it
svg.data-adjacent-source: UXLC 2.6, as copied into in/UXLC-39/: the line above, line 3, is Exodus 19:22, atom 10 of 10, and Exodus 19:23, atoms 1 to 4 of 20; the line below, line 5, is Exodus 19:23, atoms 11 to 15 of 20; the lines' words as Charles Loder's leningrad-codex-tei at commit 15405046fe811d4e1064a7ebcd7cb92261ce72db has them, which the page image agrees with
svg.data-regions-by: Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-01: re-drafted under profile 2 by a script of Claude's from the draft of the same day. Each region's ink is what a watershed on the photograph's luminance gives its seeds: the seeds of the draft's regions that were in one group, those lent to one letter, or to a sign of one written part, joined as one region; and seeds that Claude placed by eye, with the transcription in hand, in written parts that had none and near junctions. The draft's cuts and its regions in two groups are dropped. The groups' ids, kinds, owners and notes, and the supplied ink's reasons, are the draft's, but where a group's note says otherwise; an id sN in them names a stroke of the stroke-SVG. Strips of vellum whose reason says so are proposed by the script, where the boundary between two signs' regions is pale. On 2026-11-02 the ayin g30 of Exodus 19:23's atom 7 gained seeds in its right arm and its base, which the watershed had given the final mem g31.
